title: scrub reads the n of an escaped newline as the start of an email address, and --force then writes invalid JSON
foundBy: session agent, while scrubbing a Claude Code cassette recorded against a site whose CLAUDE.md holds `@AGENTS.md`
details:
The email pattern in `internal/cassette/scrub.go` runs over the file's raw bytes, where a newline is the two characters `\n`. Claude Code puts the text `\n\n@AGENTS.md` in its prompt when a project's `CLAUDE.md` imports `AGENTS.md`, and scrub reports `n@AGENTS.md` as an email address, since `md` passes as a top-level domain.

This was reproduced at `41c67be` on a Claude Code cassette of four requests. `cassette scrub` finds one email in each. With the escaped newline replaced by a space, it finds none.

With `--force` it replaces `n@AGENTS.md` with `<EMAIL>` and leaves the backslash, so each request holds `\<EMAIL>`. That is an invalid JSON escape, and Python's `json.load` refuses the file. scrub still exits 0. A real address after any escape, such as `\n` or `\t`, would be cut and corrupted the same way.

Matching on the decoded strings would avoid both. Until then, `--allow-email @AGENTS.md` lets the import through.
